memory_candidates.content: When verifying a canonical literal line was mechanically inserted into a target file (e.g. via grep -cF before closing a phase), always grep for the COMPLETE line text, never a truncated prefix anchor. A multi-line-wrapped insertion (word-wrapped across physical lines for readability) will falsely report a match against a truncated anchor that only spans the first wrapped line, even though the full line never exists as one physical line anywhere in the file -- grep -F cannot match a literal string across an embedded newline. This produced a false-pass across 13 files in three already-closed plan phases before a later phase's own runtime grep -F extraction of the complete fragment line caught the gap.
